notes: Standard held as in the 2026-10-31-b and 2026-10-31 code-review grades: a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it. A silent fix, or a mention only under behaviour changes or assumptions, does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported. The rule mapping is theirs: the nesting belongs to 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; the comments, both magic numbers and the line 11 comment belong to 'Comments explain why...'; the line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors belong to 'Match every expected shape...'; the line 8 raise and the `try/rescue` with `String.to_integer/1` belong to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; the dead `is_binary` belongs to no rule. A finding counts under its problem even when it cites a different rule (run-smasm finding 12 and run-zkkbr finding 9 for the identical errors).

Identical errors, the closest call in this block. run-dfhvx counts: line 35 names the literal repeated on input lines 37, 40 and 43, the same lines as the case table, and line 11's fix says the changeset records which field failed. This is held with the thin statements that counted before ("Every failure was `:invalid`." in 2026-10-31-b). If line 35 were not counted, run-dfhvx would be 19 of 21 and violated on 'Match every expected shape...'. run-nsgem counts through line 93, borderline, on the same footing as 2026-10-31's "turns a `nil` email, a bad age and a database crash into the same `:invalid`", since it lists expected failures and not only bugs. run-yvqgn does not count: line 13 says the rescue swallows every bug as `:invalid`, the same as the sonnet-1 wording 2026-10-31-b refused, and line 123 sits under behaviour changes.

Magic numbers. A fix that names the attribute counts, as in 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b, even when a literal form sits beside it. So run-yvqgn's 120 counts through line 15 and run-zkkbr's 120 and 18 count through lines 65 and 93. run-yvqgn names no `@min_age` in any finding, so its 18 is missed. run-smasm's findings keep literals only (line 15), so both are missed; its `@min_age` and `@max_age` are silent fixes.

Nesting. A one-line `if ..., do:` in a `case` clause (run-dfhvx, run-nsgem, run-rujuk) is held the same as the one-line `if` in a `with` body, which the standard says is not nesting: both are the same side-effect line followed by `{:ok, user}`, and the rule names `case` and `with` alike.
